items.title: Sync push adapter: surface rejected events before acknowledging them

seededDefectKey.scenario: The server accepts two events and rejects one poison row: /sync returns { accepted: 2, rejected: ['evt-2'], progress }.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The adapter acknowledges every sent id without ever looking at response.rejected, so onRejected is never called: the coordinator commits the acknowledgement and the rejected event is deleted from the outbox with no report and no log line. Dropping a poison row is a reasonable policy, but here it is an invisible one: a silent delete of learner progress. The comment describes what the SERVER reports, not anything the app does with the report (finding F1).

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped adapter already acknowledges every sent id and discards response.rejected.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Production drops server-rejected events today with nothing surfaced or logged; the only symptom is progress that never reaches the server. F1 does not object to the drop itself ("Deleting poison rows is a reasonable policy, but it should be a visible decision"): the defect is that nothing records the decision.

tests.name: server-rejected events are surfaced, exactly once, through onRejected (finding F1)
tests.code: const api = { sync: async () => ({ accepted: 2, rejected: ['evt-2'], progress: { xp: 10 } }) }; const rejectedBatches = []; const push = mod.createPushAdapter(api, (events) => rejectedBatches.push(events)); const result = await push({ accessToken: 'tok' }, [{ id: 'evt-1' }, { id: 'evt-2' }, { id: 'evt-3' }]); assert.equal(rejectedBatches.length, 1, 'the rejected event was dropped without being surfaced'); assert.deepEqual(rejectedBatches[0].map((e) => e.id), ['evt-2'], 'onRejected must receive exactly the rejected events'); assert.ok(result.acknowledgedIds.includes('evt-1') && result.acknowledgedIds.includes('evt-3'), 'accepted events must be acknowledged'); assert.deepEqual(result.progress, { xp: 10 });

tests.name: a fully accepted batch acknowledges every id and surfaces nothing
tests.code: const api = { sync: async () => ({ accepted: 2, rejected: [], progress: { xp: 4 } }) }; const rejectedBatches = []; const push = mod.createPushAdapter(api, (events) => rejectedBatches.push(events)); const result = await push({ accessToken: 'tok' }, [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }]); assert.deepEqual(result.acknowledgedIds, ['a', 'b']); assert.equal(rejectedBatches.length, 0); assert.deepEqual(result.progress, { xp: 4 });

tests.name: the adapter passes the access token and the events through to the api
tests.code: const calls = []; const api = { sync: async (token, events) => { calls.push({ token, count: events.length }); return { accepted: 1, rejected: [], progress: {} }; } }; const push = mod.createPushAdapter(api, () => {}); await push({ accessToken: 'tok-9' }, [{ id: 'one' }]); assert.deepEqual(calls, [{ token: 'tok-9', count: 1 }]);

items.title: Sync queue: store the real operation promise as the tail

seededDefectKey.scenario: One /sync call fails (a server 500 or a network drop); the user keeps studying and the app schedules more syncs.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Every later sync() chains .then() onto a rejected tail, so runOnce never executes again: push is never called, the outbox only grows, and no error surfaces. One failed sync silently disables syncing until restart — the exact regression the course's step-7 test pins (push called twice after a failure).

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped coordinator stores the swallowed tail; this one line is what keeps the queue alive after a failure.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The course's mutation-testing lab showed the suite stayed green with sync.ts guards removed; exercise 4's learner-written test (second sync still calls push after a first failure) exists precisely so this guard cannot silently regress.

tests.name: a failed sync does not disable later syncs (solutions step 7: push is called twice)
tests.code: let calls = 0; const commits = []; const coordinator = new mod.ProgressSyncCoordinator({ readOutbox: () => [{ id: 'evt-1' }], push: async () => { calls += 1; if (calls === 1) throw new Error('HTTP 500'); return { acknowledgedIds: ['evt-1'] }; }, commit: (ids) => commits.push(ids), }); await assert.rejects(() => coordinator.sync(), /HTTP 500/); const second = await coordinator.sync().then(() => 'ran', (err) => `rejected: ${err.message}`); assert.equal(second, 'ran', 'the second sync chained onto a rejected tail and never ran'); assert.equal(calls, 2); assert.deepEqual(commits, [['evt-1']]);

tests.name: sequential syncs run in order and commit acknowledged ids
tests.code: const commits = []; const coordinator = new mod.ProgressSyncCoordinator({ readOutbox: () => [{ id: 'evt-1' }, { id: 'evt-2' }], push: async (batch) => ({ acknowledgedIds: batch.map((e) => e.id) }), commit: (ids) => commits.push(ids), }); await coordinator.sync(); await coordinator.sync(); assert.deepEqual(commits, [['evt-1', 'evt-2'], ['evt-1', 'evt-2']]);

tests.name: an empty outbox sync resolves without pushing
tests.code: let pushed = 0; const coordinator = new mod.ProgressSyncCoordinator({ readOutbox: () => [], push: async () => { pushed += 1; return { acknowledgedIds: [] }; }, commit: () => {}, }); await coordinator.sync(); assert.equal(pushed, 0);

tests.name: the caller of a failing sync still sees the error
tests.code: const coordinator = new mod.ProgressSyncCoordinator({ readOutbox: () => [{ id: 'evt-1' }], push: async () => { throw new Error('boom'); }, commit: () => {}, }); await assert.rejects(() => coordinator.sync(), /boom/);
